circle_window_thinker_v1: Variant 1 thinker for the ending credits (scene F7). Each frame: SetEntryHere re-entry, HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1 (which rebuilds only when the parameters changed), then QueueHdma of the buffer selected by chatPtr bit 0 (odd = $7E7000, even = $7E7100) on channel config #26 (WH0/WH1). It never zeroes the previous-parameter copies and never restores them, so while the radius is not negative the builder's use of $FC as a decision variable makes the next frame see a change: the table is rebuilt every frame and the buffers alternate every frame.
circle_window_thinker_v2: Variant 2 thinker for the Gold Ship dream (scene 2A) and the Mu vampire lair (scene 67). HdmaInitPrevState clears the previous centre X, centre Y and radius once (so the first frame builds only if one of the current centre X, centre Y or radius is non-zero); then every frame: HdmaCompareParams, and only on a change HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2 and HdmaCopyCurrentToPrev (which also restores $FC from $FE); finally QueueHdma of the buffer chosen by chatPtr bit 0 on channel config #26. An unchanged circle keeps re-queueing the same buffer.
CircleNextRowV1: Bresenham row step inside HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1: advances Y offset $1C (by 2 on first entry), writes WH0/WH1 word pairs for symmetric rows, and loops until x drops below y or goes negative, else jumps back from the loop tail.
CircleNextRowV2: Row step inside HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2: increments $1C, emits hold/repeat HDMA segments for above- and below-centre rows while y stays in range, then returns to the x/y loop or exits to HdmaCircleWindowExitV2.
CircleWindowV1Entry: Credits circle-window thinker frame entry: SetEntryHere, HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1, then QueueHdma on config $26 using buffer A at tileStagingBuffer or B at $7E7100 based on chatPtr bit 0.
CircleWindowV2Entry: Dream and vampire-lair thinker entry: HdmaInitPrevState once, then each frame HdmaCompareParams skips rebuild when unchanged, else HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2 and HdmaCopyCurrentToPrev, then QueueHdma with the same buffer select as V1.
HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1:
Variant 1 circle builder (credits only). Same flow as HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2: HdmaParamChangeCheck (changed -> build, unchanged -> exit), default table (one empty line, end marker), negative radius exits, then the Bresenham loop with $18 = x, $1C = y and $FC = decision variable, filling words (left = centreX - half-width, right = centreX + half-width, clamped to a byte) into the row data and emitting hold / repeat segments.
Differences from V2, all in the row arithmetic: the line counts are computed in half resolution (hold lines = (2 x centre Y - radius) / 2, circle lines = radius + 1, so the vertical extent is half of V2's 2 x radius + 1); data rows are addressed with a one-byte stride (index = $00 +- y) and each row is stored as a word, so neighbouring rows overwrite each other's second byte, while the repeat-mode entries read one word per line and advance the data pointer by 2 bytes; the "centre above the screen" tests of V2 are missing; and x is decreased by 2 instead of 1 when the decision variable goes negative. V1 therefore does not produce the same table as V2 for the same parameters. Its visible result in the credits (centre $80, $7F, radius up to $3F) is unverified (open question).
On exit it restores DBR, D and X. It does not copy the parameters to the previous state; HdmaParamChangeCheck has already done that, apart from $FC, which stays at the final decision value.
HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2:
Variant 2 circle builder (Gold Ship dream, Mu vampire lair). Runs with D = 0 and DBR = $7E. Steps: (1) HdmaParamChangeCheck stores the previous parameters, toggles the buffer and sets $00 (data centre), $02 (table write pointer) and $04 (empty word address). (2) A default table is written first: one line of empty window and the end marker, so a switched-off circle (negative radius) leaves a valid table. (3) The radius is rounded to even and becomes $18 (x), $FC (decision variable) and $1A (x as a clamped byte). (4) Empty lines above the circle: centre Y - radius lines go out through HdmaEmitHoldSegments; if the circle is cut off by the top of the screen (or the centre is above it) the data pointer starts at the first visible row instead, and a circle that ends above the screen emits nothing. (5) HdmaEmitRepeatSegments emits 2 x radius + 1 repeat lines over the row data. (6) A final one-line empty entry and the end marker follow. (7) The Bresenham loop fills the row data: $1C = y, $1E = y clamped to a byte, rows centre + y and centre - y, then the transposed octant; each word is (left, right) = centreX -/+ half-width clamped to 0 / 255, written with the right edge in the high byte for WH1.
Row data uses 2 bytes per scanline (ASL of the row offset); rows with an offset of $100 or more are skipped.
HdmaCircleWindowExitV1: Restore path for HdmaCircleWindowBuildV1: PLB, PLD, PLX and return; taken when parameters unchanged, radius negative, or the Bresenham loop finishes.
HdmaCircleWindowExitV2: Restore path for HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2: same register restore and return; also reached when HdmaParamChangeCheck reports no parameter change or radius is negative.
HdmaCompareParams: Compare the previous parameters ($F4/$F8/$FC) with the current ones ($F6/$FA/$FE): centre X, centre Y, radius. All equal -> RTS with the carry that the last CMP left set; any difference -> CLC. The caller (circle_window_thinker_v2) branches on carry set = unchanged.
HdmaCopyCurrentToPrev: Previous parameters = current parameters (centre X $F6 -> $F4, centre Y $FA -> $F8, radius $FE -> $FC). This also restores $FC, which HdmaCircleWindowBuildV2 used as its decision variable.
HdmaEmitHoldSegments: Emit hold entries for the lines above the circle. In: A = line count, Z set when A is zero; $04 = data pointer; Y = table write pointer. Each loop writes one 3-byte entry (count 1-127, pointer = $04, the shared empty-window word), subtracts the count from the remainder (kept on the stack) and repeats until nothing is left; the Z flag of the final PLA ends the loop. Count bit 7 stays clear, so HDMA holds the one word for the whole segment. These are the lines above the circle.
HdmaEmitRepeatSegments: Emit the circle's repeat-mode entries. In: A = line count (Z set when zero); $02 = pointer to the first row-data word of the first segment; Y = table write pointer. Each loop writes a 3-byte entry whose count byte is (count | $80), so HDMA reads a new data word on every scanline of the segment, with the data pointer in $02; $02 then advances by count x 2 bytes (one word per line). Segments are capped at 127 lines. Bit 7 is HDMA's repeat flag, not a direction flag: the old comment ("direction bit, upward") was wrong.
HdmaInitPrevState: Zero the previous centre X ($F4), centre Y ($F8) and radius ($FC) so that the first HdmaCompareParams of circle_window_thinker_v2 reports a change whenever the scene has set any non-zero parameter.
HdmaNoChange: Return with carry set: the parameters did not change.
HdmaParamChangeCheck: Compare the current parameters with the ones used for the last build: radius $FE against $FC, centre X $F6 against $F4, centre Y $FA against $F8. All equal -> HdmaNoChange (carry set, nothing else happens). Any difference -> all three previous copies are updated, chatPtr,X is incremented and the table state is set for the buffer that bit 0 selects: odd = buffer A (row data centre $7600 in $00, table $7000 in $02), even = buffer B ($7A00 and $7100); in both cases $7E7200 receives the empty-window word $00FF and $04 = $7200. Returns carry clear = rebuild. The comparison order is radius, centre X, centre Y, and the stores use the entry point of the first field that differs, so every later field is refreshed too.
